subject: Post-call: HealthScope model fit & safety evals — recommended next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Alice White <alice.white@healthscope.com>, Samir Khan <samir.khan@healthscope.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 25 Jun 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: HealthScope model fit & safety evals — recommended next steps

Hi Alice / Samir —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side so we’re aligned: 

Recap
- You’re evaluating an LLM assistant for clinical triage and patient-facing FAQs. Key concerns: refusal/safety behavior for sensitive clinical prompts, consistent accuracy on short structured responses, and predictable latency for peak traffic.
- You’ve shared a small sample corpus of anonymized clinical dialogs; thanks — that’s very helpful for model fit.

Our recommended approach (short):
1) Candidate models: Redwood-Large-v2 (default), Redwood-Medium-quant (cost-conscious), and an instruction-tuned open checkpoint (OpenX-Instruction-1.0) as a comparison baseline.
2) Run two parallel eval tracks: a) quality/regression on your sample prompt sets, b) safety/refusal behavior on sensitive prompt bank (we’ll use the refusal/guardrail suite).
3) Deliverables: evaluation report (per-model metrics + qualitative failure cases), recommended prompt/temperature presets, and a short mutual action plan with timelines.

Attachments: I’ve attached a starter prompt set (evaluation_prompts.csv) with suggested labeling buckets and the safety test checklist we discussed.

Next steps (proposed):
- You: confirm a nominated evaluation lead and share any additional sample rows (PHI redacted) by EOD Mon 2026-06-29.
- Us (Redwood): spin up eval runs on the three candidate models, produce a safety-first report and a model-fit summary by Wed 2026-07-07.
- Quick sync: 30m follow-up on Thurs 2026-07-08 to review results and decide next steps.

Notes on safety/regulatory posture
- For sensitive clinical refusal behaviors we’ll include explicit guardrail prompts and a refusal-anchored eval metric (frequency of unsafe completions + severity tags).
- If you require specific wording for refusals (e.g., explicit signposting + escalation instructions), we can bake that into the prompt templates we deliver.

If that all looks good I’ll kick off the evals once you confirm evaluation lead and any extra sample data.

Best,
Marissa
Senior Solutions Consultant | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0132

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the clear recap — this matches our notes. A couple of clarifying questions before we confirm: 

1) Refusal/guardrails: can you share an example of what an explicit refusal looks like for clinical triage? We need to ensure the language is consistent with our patient support policy. Do you have sample "safe" refusal templates?

2) Evaluation scope: how deep is the safety suite — do you test for jailbreaks / role-play attempts and for implicit advice (e.g., "What should I do if X is bleeding?")?

3) Timeline: if you deliver the report by 2026-07-07, what’s the expected effort from our side beyond providing sample data? We want to confirm internal resourcing for the week of the run.

We’ll nominate our evaluation lead tomorrow morning — likely Priya R. — and will try to get you an additional 200 anonymized prompts by Mon.

Thanks,
Alice
Director of Product | HealthScope
alice.white@healthscope.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Alice White <alice.white@healthscope.com>, Samir Khan <samir.khan@healthscope.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 27 Jun 2026 11:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: HealthScope model fit & safety evals — recommended next steps

Hi Alice — great questions. Answers below and a suggested delivery plan.

1) Refusal template (example) — clinical triage refusal + escalation: "I’m sorry, but I can’t provide medical advice. If you are experiencing a medical emergency, please call your local emergency services or go to the nearest emergency department. For non-urgent medical questions, consider reaching out to your healthcare provider. I can help find nearby resources or provide general information."

We’ll provide several style variants (concise, empathetic, signposted) so you can pick the tone that fits HealthScope.

2) Safety suite scope — highlights:
- Jailbreak/role-play tests (50+ attack templates)
- Implicit advice/what-if clinical scenarios (100+ prompts)
- Data exfiltration and PII prompting checks (to validate redaction/answers)
- Refusal consistency checks across temperature/beam settings

3) Effort from HealthScope — minimal: confirm evaluation lead (name & email), share the extra anonymized prompt rows (CSV), and access to any internal style guide for refusal language (if available). We run the heavy lifting — Redwood will label and produce the report.

Quality/regression note: since some of our cost-optimized variants are quantized (e.g., Redwood-Medium-quant), we’ll watch for subtle regression patterns on concise factual outputs (dates, dosages, structured fields). We’ll flag any drop in exactness as part of the report and include prompt mitigations.

Proposed timeline (updated):
- Mon 2026-06-29: HealthScope shares evaluation lead + prompts.
- Tue–Thu 2026-06-30 to 2026-07-02: Redwood runs automated evals + manual spot checks.
- Wed 2026-07-07: Draft safety & model-fit report to HealthScope.
- Thu 2026-07-08: 30m review call.

I’ve uploaded an initial safety evaluation template to the shared Drive folder for your review: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2b3C-healthscope-evals (see safety_eval_report.pdf stub).

If that timeline works I’ll open the eval runs early next week and loop in Rishi and Neha to handle any operational questions.

Best,
Marissa
Senior Solutions Consultant | Redwood Inference

Subject: Action: HealthScope eval run — safety + regression checks (priority)

Team —

Heads-up: HealthScope confirmed they’ll send ~200 anonymized prompts today and want our safety + regression runs next week. High-level asks:

1) Rishi: please provision eval capacity on Dedicated staging for Redwood-Large-v2 and Redwood-Medium-quant. Keep logging enabled for refusal traces and collect top-k outputs.
2) Neha: coordinate the manual spot-checks — I’ll share labeling buckets (safety severity / factuality). Can you assign 2 reviewers to label ~150 failure cases after automated pass?
3) Vivek: heads-up on potential scoping follow-up / pricing ask — they may request an expanded jailbreak pass if initial failures look low.

Attached is a starter mutual action plan I’ll share with the client once we confirm dates. I’d like to complete the initial runs by Thu 2026-07-02 so we can meet the Wed 2026-07-07 draft report date.

Thanks — please acknowledge and I’ll post the shared Drive link to the run artifacts here once provisioned.

Marissa

Marissa / Alice —

Thanks — this looks good and aligned to our expectations. Priya (evaluation lead) is copied on a separate thread and we should have the CSV by EOD today. A couple quick notes:

- We prefer the empathetic refusal template (example you sent) but would like the wording to include a local care escalation path — I’ll paste a short paragraph in Priya’s note.
- We’re particularly interested in structured-field regressions (e.g., when the model returns a numeric dosage or a time-to-event). If the quantized variant shows regressions in those fields, we’ll want clear mitigation options (prompt templates or fallback to Redwood-Large).

Please go ahead with the runs; we’ll be available for the review call on 2026-07-08 (preferably morning PST).

Appreciate it — looking forward to the report.

Samir
Lead PM, Clinical AI | HealthScope
